cards.title: Physiology of the autonomic nervous system
cards.byline: McCorry LK. American Journal of Pharmaceutical Education.
cards.scope: Background on autonomic pathways and organ functions, including parasympathetic control. This is not a trial of a relaxation technique or of Neuvago.

cards.title: Autonomic determinism: the modes of autonomic control, the doctrine of autonomic space, and the laws of autonomic constraint
cards.byline: Berntson GG, Cacioppo JT, Quigley KS. Psychological Review.
cards.scope: Explains why sympathetic and parasympathetic control cannot be reduced to opposite ends of a single scale. It is not a way to diagnose an individual from how calm they feel.

cards.title: Toward understanding respiratory sinus arrhythmia: relations to cardiac vagal tone, evolution and biobehavioral functions
cards.byline: Grossman P, Taylor EW. Biological Psychology.
cards.scope: Discusses how breathing, physical activity and other factors affect the interpretation of respiratory sinus arrhythmia as an index of cardiac vagal tone. It is not a whole-vagus health test.

cards.title: Heart rate variability and sympathovagal balance: pharmacological validation
cards.byline: Bootsma et al.. Netherlands Heart Journal.
cards.scope: Examines HRV measures against pharmacological autonomic blockade. This laboratory study does not validate a consumer score for resilience, recovery or general vagus-nerve health.

cards.title: Freeze for action: neurobiological mechanisms in animal and human freezing
cards.byline: Roelofs K. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
cards.scope: Reviews animal and human research on defensive freezing and preparation for action. Freezing in this literature is not simply another word for tiredness, low motivation or emotional numbness.

cards.title: Fear and the Defense Cascade: Clinical Implications and Management
cards.byline: Kozlowska K, Walker P, McLean L, Carrive P. Harvard Review of Psychiatry.
cards.scope: Distinguishes defensive responses including freezing and tonic or collapsed immobility. Its clinical framework is not a self-diagnosis checklist or evidence for a Neuvago treatment effect.

cards.title: Advances in recovery research: What have we learned? What should be done next?
cards.byline: Sonnentag S, Venz L, Casper A. Journal of Occupational Health Psychology.
cards.scope: Reviews recovery from job stress during nonwork time. This is background on employee well-being, not a clinical test for persistent fatigue or proof that one routine restores the nervous system.

cards.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain
cards.byline: McEwen BS. Physiological Reviews.
cards.scope: Describes adaptive and maladaptive stress responses involving multiple body systems. It does not measure an individual’s stress load from symptoms or establish that a stress response must be completed by a particular technique.

cards.title: Hyperarousal and sleep reactivity in insomnia: current insights
cards.byline: Kalmbach DA et al. Nature and Science of Sleep.
cards.scope: Discusses arousal and sensitivity of sleep to stress in insomnia research, with uncertainty about specific mechanisms. This does not diagnose insomnia or a nervous-system problem from the feeling of being tired but alert.

cards.title: The perseverative cognition hypothesis: a review of worry, prolonged stress-related physiological activation, and health
cards.byline: Brosschot JF, Gerin W, Thayer JF. Journal of Psychosomatic Research.
cards.scope: Reviews preliminary support for worry and rumination prolonging stress-related activation. It is a proposed explanation, not a universal cause of symptoms or evidence that stress is trapped in the body.

cards.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain
cards.byline: McEwen BS. Physiological Reviews.
cards.scope: Describes adaptive and maladaptive stress responses involving multiple body systems. It does not measure an individual’s stress load from symptoms or establish that a stress response must be completed by a particular technique.

cards.title: The perseverative cognition hypothesis: a review of worry, prolonged stress-related physiological activation, and health
cards.byline: Brosschot JF, Gerin W, Thayer JF. Journal of Psychosomatic Research.
cards.scope: Reviews preliminary support for worry and rumination prolonging stress-related activation. It is a proposed explanation, not a universal cause of symptoms or evidence that stress is trapped in the body.

cards.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain
cards.byline: McEwen BS. Physiological Reviews.
cards.scope: Describes stress and adaptation across neural, endocrine and other body systems. It does not validate this page as a symptom checklist or diagnose autonomic dysfunction from everyday experiences.

cards.title: Measures of emotion: A review
cards.byline: Mauss IB, Robinson MD. Cognition and Emotion.
cards.scope: Examines subjective, physiological and behavioural measures of emotion and why they are not interchangeable. It does not establish that feeling calm measures vagal tone or nervous-system health.

cards.title: Measures of emotion: A review
cards.byline: Mauss IB, Robinson MD. Cognition and Emotion.
cards.scope: Examines subjective, physiological and behavioural measures of emotion and why they are not interchangeable. It does not establish that feeling calm measures vagal tone or nervous-system health.

cards.title: Emotion regulation: affective, cognitive, and social consequences
cards.byline: Gross JJ. Psychophysiology.
cards.scope: Reviews reappraisal and suppression, with different consequences for emotional experience, expression and physiology. It is not a universal prescription to suppress feelings, a diagnostic tool or a study of Neuvago.

cards.title: Emotion regulation: affective, cognitive, and social consequences
cards.byline: Gross JJ. Psychophysiology.
cards.scope: Reviews reappraisal and suppression, with different consequences for emotional experience, expression and physiology. It is not a universal prescription to suppress feelings, a diagnostic tool or a study of Neuvago.

cards.title: Emotion-regulation strategies across psychopathology: A meta-analytic review
cards.byline: Aldao A, Nolen-Hoeksema S, Schweizer S. Clinical Psychology Review.
cards.scope: Synthesises associations between emotion-regulation strategies and mental-health symptoms. Associations vary across samples and do not establish an individual diagnosis, a single cause or a product treatment effect.

cards.title: Anxiety disorders
cards.byline: World Health Organization. WHO fact sheet.
cards.scope: Overview of anxiety disorders, their impact and available care. This is general information, not a diagnostic test or evidence for a Neuvago treatment effect.

cards.title: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults: management
cards.byline: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE clinical guideline CG113.
cards.scope: Assessment and care options for adults with generalised anxiety disorder or panic disorder. It does not cover every anxiety presentation and is not a self-treatment protocol.

cards.title: Burn-out an occupational phenomenon: International Classification of Diseases
cards.byline: World Health Organization. WHO ICD-11 clarification.
cards.scope: Defines burnout in an occupational context and distinguishes its ICD-11 classification from a medical condition. This does not make exhaustion outside work unimportant or remove the need for care.

cards.title: Understanding the burnout experience: recent research and its implications for psychiatry
cards.byline: Maslach C, Leiter MP. World Psychiatry.
cards.scope: Reviews occupational burnout, measurement and its relationship with mental health. It is not a trial of Neuvago and does not establish a single biological test or universal recovery plan.

cards.title: Mental health at work
cards.byline: World Health Organization. WHO fact sheet.
cards.scope: Describes workplace risks and organisational responses alongside individual support. These recommendations concern mental health at work broadly, not proof that a particular routine treats burnout.
